definition: Cycle of violence refers to the way violence can be passed from one generation to the next, so that exposure to violence in the family, such as interparental violence, is linked to a higher likelihood of later experiencing intimate partner violence. In this sense, early exposure can help sustain violence across relationships and over time.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly support the framing that violence is “passed from one generation to the next” as a definitional mechanism; it only mentions an “intergenerational cycle of violence” and that women exposed to interparental violence had a higher likelihood of experiencing IPV.

The definition’s claim that exposure to violence in the family is linked to a “higher likelihood of later experiencing intimate partner violence” is only partially supported: the packet states that “married women exposed to interparental violence … had a higher likelihood of experiencing intimate partner violence,” but it does not clearly establish the “later”/time-sequence aspect needed for the definition.
The claim that “early exposure can help sustain violence across relationships and over time” is not directly supported in the provided packet text.
